headline: Deep models gain experimental restraints and geometric priors for biomolecular design
label: Deep Learning Biomolecular Design
summary: Recent preprints pair pretrained structure and language models with XL-MS, HDX-MS, and surface-geometry constraints for design and prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned generative and predictive modeling of biomolecular structure, function, and stability, spanning diffusion and flow-matching co-folding and ligand generation, protein language models, and equivariant or graph networks. What is new in several items is the explicit injection of experimental data and physical or geometric priors into these models. AIMS-Fold steers pretrained diffusion-based co-folding with differentiable XL-MS and HDX-MS restraints, SwitchCraft backpropagates through compositional constraints to design state-switching proteins, and SurfDesign conditions design on molecular surface geometry. ProtEGNN pairs PLM embeddings with an E(3)-equivariant graph network, while SILO applies oracle-budgeted trajectory search. The set is heterogeneous: TadA-Bench and AutoScientists address benchmarking and agentic workflow rather than this modeling pattern.
